newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Bunce offered 2-year contract by NZRFU.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Bunce offered 2-year contract by NZRFU.

text.p: Veteran All Black centre Frank Bunce has been offered a new two-year contract by the New Zealand Rugby Football Union, NZPA reported on Wednesday.

Bunce, New Zealand's most capped rugby centre with 43 test appearances, is also the oldest player in the side and isn't committing himself past 1997 as the All Blacks build towards the World Cup in Wales in two years time.

He is also well aware of form Super 12 players like Auckland's Eroni Clarke, who has just signed an upgraded deal with the New Zealand Rugby Football Union (NZRFU), signing up for a further four years, and Wellington Hurricane Alama
Ieremia, who are putting pressure on his test spot.

Bunce said the two-year NZRFU contract, taking him through to 2000, came at a time when he was contemplating his international future, although he probably wouldn't give it much thought until the end of this season.

"It's nice to see they're not putting me out to pasture just yet but if I was to retire from international rugby this year the opportunity might be there just to play Super 12 and NPC rugby," he said.
The former Western Samoan international was concentrating on recovering from a foot injury that had curbed his involvement in the later stages of the Waikato Chiefs' Super 12 campaign.
The 35-year-old is disappointed at the Chiefs' failure to fire this season but rejects speculation of a rift between the side's two main feeder unions -- Waikato and North Harbour.

"Sure, there's no escaping the fact that we come from different areas, with a mix of rural and those of us from the city but the team has come together well and the atmosphere is as good if not better than any team I've been with."

Bunce believes the team's decline this season can be traced back to the shock defeat at the hands of the Canterbury Crusaders -- "the only game this season where I think we played badly for almost the full 80 minutes.

"I think that result really affected the players mentally and although we've won since, I'm not sure that we fully recovered from the feeling in the changing room afterwards, with possibly a few doubts creeping in whenever we've run out onto the field since."
Bunce is eager to be involved in another winning All Black season but knows the acid is on from coach John Hart for everyone to lift their performances for the international arena.

"I'm well aware that there are some form players around but I don't mind the pressure and actually believe I thrive on it. I think I've got my foot in the door but I never take anything for granted." -- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
